title: The Wrong House
premise: Lena Nakamura takes a teaching post in the fog-bound town of Grayhollow, where students vanish one by one and the staff's polite silence curdles into complicity. When she rents a cheap room in the old Halloway house, its mirrors begin lagging a second behind reality — reflections that eventually stop copying her at all. She discovers the house was 'invited' decades ago by the school's founding families, who traded children for prosperity, and that her predecessor teacher died holding the door shut from inside. To survive until sunrise, Lena must refuse every bargain the house offers — including the one that would return her dead brother to her — and instead break the invitation itself, an act that costs her the reflection she came in with. She walks out at dawn unrecognizable even to herself, carrying the town's ledger of names as both evidence and inheritance.
about_author: Beatrix Halloran is the pen name of a former night-shift archivist who spent years cataloguing the belongings of the unclaimed dead. Her fiction is known for quiet dread, domestic hauntings, and protagonists who mistake stubbornness for courage.

chapters.title: One-Way Ticket
chapters.summary: Lena arrives in Grayhollow by bus, fleeing a career scandal and her brother Daniel's funeral. POV: Lena. The town is too welcoming; the school too eager. Emotional beat: wary hope masking grief, establishing her reflexive disbelief in anything she can't grade.

chapters.title: Attendance Is Mandatory
chapters.summary: Lena's first week teaching; she notices empty desks no one acknowledges and a seating chart with names crossed out in red. Principal Voss deflects smoothly. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: professional unease hardening into suspicion as colleagues perform normalcy too well.

chapters.title: The Room at the End of the Hall
chapters.summary: Lena rents a room in the Halloway house from landlady Mrs. Okafor, who has odd rules: cover the hallway mirror after dark, never answer knocks before dawn. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the comfort of a bargain priced just below what she can afford.

chapters.title: Second Behind
chapters.summary: Lena catches her reflection moving a beat late — first dismissible as tiredness, then undeniable when the mirror shows her doorway before she opens it. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a rational mind watching its own rules fail.

chapters.title: What the Students Know
chapters.summary: A surviving student, Marcus Ito, slips Lena a note listing vanished classmates and one word: invited. He begs her not to stay past October. POV: alternating Lena and Marcus. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being believed for the first time.

chapters.title: The Predecessor's Desk
chapters.summary: Lena finds her missing predecessor Ruth Calloway's lesson plans hidden in a desk drawer, ending mid-sentence with instructions: don't look at your face after midnight; count the doors twice. POV: Lena reading Ruth's voice. Emotional beat: dread inherited like a hand-me-down.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: At the school's parent night, Lena meets the founding families — the Ashcombes, the Veres — whose portraits hang above the auditorium and whose eyes follow her. They offer help finding 'whatever's troubling you.' POV: Lena. Emotional beat: charm as a predator's patience.

chapters.title: Daniel at the Window
chapters.summary: The mirror shows Daniel, alive, waving from the yard. Lena nearly goes down; only Okafor's rule stops her. The house begins speaking in his voice through the walls. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: grief weaponized, temptation sharpened into a blade.

chapters.title: Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: In the basement, Lena finds a ledger: generations of children traded by name, each entry signed by a founding family, the most recent signature fresh ink — Voss. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: horror reorganized into pattern, which is worse than chaos.

chapters.title: Marcus Doesn't Come to School
chapters.summary: Marcus vanishes; his desk appears on the red-inked chart overnight. Lena confronts Voss, who admits the arrangement exists and offers her immunity if she stops digging. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into resolve; survival versus complicity.

chapters.title: The House Remembers Her
chapters.summary: The mirrors now show a version of Lena who stayed — older, hollow-eyed, still teaching in an empty classroom. The house insists this is mercy: a life preserved forever. POV: Lena and her reflection in counterpoint. Emotional beat: identity fraying at the seams.

chapters.title: Okafor's Confession
chapters.summary: Mrs. Okafor reveals she was a taken child returned wrong — the reason for her rules — and that the invitation can be broken only inside the house, before sunrise, by someone the house wants. POV: Okafor then Lena. Emotional beat: two survivors recognizing each other across decades of damage.

chapters.title: Count the Doors Twice
chapters.summary: Lena maps the house at dusk and counts thirteen doors where twelve existed that morning. The extra one breathes. Ruth's notes warn: it opens for whoever answers it. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: claustrophobic escalation; the geometry of trust collapsing.

chapters.title: The Bargain Offered
chapters.summary: The founding families gather in her room without knocking, offering Daniel back, her reputation restored, tenure forever — all she must do is renew the invitation with her signature. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit and almost reasonable.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Lena says no. The house stops pretending: doors relocate, mirrors multiply, and the lagged reflections begin acting independently, hunting her through rooms that rearrange. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into clarity — fear is the house's currency, and she stops paying.

chapters.title: Ruth's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Following Ruth's final note, Lena finds the original invitation nailed beneath the hearthstone, written in the blood-signatures of the founders. The house floods her mind with every taken child's voice begging her to sign instead. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: compassion under siege; mercy twisted into a trap.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Door Opens
chapters.summary: Cornered, Lena faces the thirteenth door, behind which Daniel stands real or near enough. She opens it — but steps through as herself, refusing the trade, dragging the door off its hinges into the hall. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the climax's pivot — courage defined as walking toward grief without accepting its terms.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: With the door broken, the house unravels; the founders scream as their signatures burn off the page. Lena must hold the torn door against the dark until dawn while the taken children pass through her, going home or going free. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: endurance as love; the longest hour of her life.

chapters.title: Aftermath, First Period
chapters.summary: Dawn. The house is ordinary; the mirrors are only mirrors. At school, Voss is gone and Marcus is back, remembering nothing. Lena reads the class attendance aloud and every name answers present. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: fragile, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: The Missing Reflection
chapters.summary: Okafor shows Lena the truth of the cost: the mirrors show the room perfectly — except for her. The part of her the house kept was her image, her old self. POV: Lena and Okafor. Emotional beat: mourning a self that survived in name only.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Lena delivers the ledger to a state investigator and learns the founding families were people all along — the horror needed human hands. She testifies, naming names, becoming the town's conscience whether it wants one or not. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: power refused, then reclaimed as responsibility.

chapters.title: Present Tense
chapters.summary: Months later, Lena stays in Grayhollow, teaching. A new student transfers in with a familiar last name, and the hallway mirror — replaced, new glass — hesitates half a heartbeat. Lena covers it with her coat and keeps walking. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: vigilance as a way of life; survival is not an ending but a practice.
